subject: Next steps: Secure deployment requirements & technical workshop
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@reguhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & recap from today's secure deployment discovery

Hi Anna — thanks again for a great conversation today. Quick recap while it's fresh, and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of pain & goals we captured
- Primary pain: inconsistent latency under peak workloads and no reliable isolation model for sensitive PHI-based requests.
- Compliance: ReguHealth needs customer-managed key control (KMS/HSM) + audit logs retained 7 years and evidence for SOC2-type controls.
- Network constraints: production environment must be able to run in a VPC with controlled egress; optional air-gap consideration for certain environments.
- Success criteria (what would make this a win): predictable 99th perc latency under 400ms for conversational flows, keys managed by ReguHealth KMS/HSM with no plaintext persisted in Redwood systems, and formal acceptance of a Milestone-based PoC.

Current stack notes you shared
- Primary inference clients in AWS us-west-2.
- Existing KMS: HashiCorp Vault (Enterprise) + AWS KMS for some services.
- Deployment preference: customer-managed VPC with peering or private link; limited public internet egress preferred.

Technical unknowns we flagged
- Do you require full air-gapped deployment (no outbound) or is restricted egress acceptable for signing/certs?
- Any specific FIPS/NIST validation requirements for HSMs?
- Expected peak concurrent sessions and average sequence length for predictions (tokens)?

Proposed next steps (owners & rough dates)
1) Technical workshop with your infra & security (90 min) — proposed Wed Sep 29 09:00 PT — Owner: Ben / Marissa (please confirm availability)
2) Redwood to share architecture sketch + preliminary KMS integration patterns — 48 hours after workshop — Owner: Marissa
3) ReguHealth to send completed MAL/ops requirements sheet (we'll attach a template) — Owner: Anna / Tom — due Fri Oct 1
4) Schedule procurement touchpoint once baseline pricing & scope are aligned — Owner: Procurement / Ben — target week of Oct 4

Attachments: I attached a lightweight architecture sketch and our security snapshot for your team to review. Also dropping our PoC template link below.

If I missed anything or mischaracterized a requirement, please call it out — otherwise I'll plan to lock the workshop time once you confirm.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

- redwood-security-snapshot.pdf (2 pages)

Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 17:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & recap from today's secure deployment discovery

Thanks Ben — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We are leaning toward a VPC deployment with no public IPs on inference hosts and tightly controlled egress. Full air-gap is on the table for certain environments but needs feasibility review (we'll confirm which workloads).
- Vault (HashiCorp) is the canonical KMS for us; we do have a FIPS-validated HSM in our catalog (Thales) for keys that must be hardware-backed.
- For sizing: expect 300-500 concurrent chat sessions at peak, median request ~ 150 tokens, burst to 400 tokens for extended context.

We'll fill out the MAL sheet you attached and return by Oct 1. Wed Sep 29 09:00 PT works for our infra and security (Tom). Adding Tom here so he can field the technical questions.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Anna Lopez
Head of Product Security | ReguHealth
anna.lopez@reguhealth.com | +1 (650) 555-0199
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@reguhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & recap from today's secure deployment discovery

Hi Anna / Ben — jumping in with a couple technical clarifications so our workshop can be focused: 

1) KMS/HSM: Redwood supports integrating with customer-managed KMS via standard KMIP and can broker envelope keys with your Vault + Thales HSM. We need certificate pinning and a staging credential exchange during PoC.
2) Network: we support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and can run in a customer-provisioned subnet with NAT restrictions. For fully air-gapped, we'll need to discuss an on-prem package and offline signing procedures.
3) Logging: we can forward audit logs to your S3/GCS endpoint and support 7+ year retention via lifecycle policies; we'll mark what data remains within your control vs Redwood-managed metadata.

For the workshop I'd like to cover three demo artifacts: 1) KMS handshake flow, 2) sample routing/fallback policies for model variants, and 3) KV cache isolation patterns. If there are any network diagrams or ACLs you can share ahead of time, please attach them — will save us time.

I'll prep the architecture sketch and a short runbook we can iterate on. Ben — I'll upload the files to the shared drive once ready.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Anna / Tom — quick tech checklist to help us prepare the workshop. Please reply inline where possible.

1) VPC details: CIDR ranges, existing peering or Transit Gateway? (answer: )
2) Allowed outbound federated endpoints (if any) — e.g., CRLs, OCSP, cert download? (answer: )
3) Vault access pattern: TLS endpoints, service account for Redwood PoC agents, ACL policy that allows encrypt/decrypt? (answer: )
4) HSM: PKCS#11 or network HSM? Model signing or key wrapping preference? (answer: )
5) Storage for audit logs: S3 bucket ARN + expected KMS key for server-side encryption? (answer: )
6) Maintenance windows & timezones for scheduled restarts (answer: )

If you can paste the answers before Mon Sep 27 12:00 PT, Marissa and I can draft the PoC environment and a minimal config that matches your constraints.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.
